summary: Ten comment-endorsed developer tools, research projects, museums, and a book from 30 fully crawled HN threads.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: ATEN CS782DP
items.summary: A 4K DisplayPort KVM switch for sharing peripherals between two computers.
items.why_included: A long-term user said it does the job for switching work and personal machines.
items.evidence: The user endorsed the KVM while noting occasional reconnection problems.

evidence_sources.author: noelwelsh
evidence_sources.excerpt: I have an ATEN KVM [1] that gets a solid "it does the job" from me.

items.name: Mjolnir
items.source_story_title: AgentsDock: An IDE designed for agentic AI research
items.summary: An agent workspace with containers, EC2 support, and portable sessions.
items.why_included: A commenter directly recommended it to software engineers evaluating agent research environments.
items.evidence: The recommendation highlighted built-in containerization and session portability across machines and harnesses.

evidence_sources.author: jbellis
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you're more of a SWE than a data scientist, check out Mjolnir:

items.name: Maturin / PyO3
items.source_story_title: Libraries Run Rust Inside Python (With PyO3)
items.summary: Rust tooling for building Python packages and portable manylinux wheels.
items.why_included: A developer uses the combination to make Rust software easy for Python users to install.
items.evidence: The developer praised automatic manylinux builds as a practical answer to Linux ABI fragmentation.

evidence_sources.author: the__alchemist
evidence_sources.excerpt: Bonus: Maturin/PyO3 can build "manylinux" binaries automatically, which helps with the Linux ABI diaspora.

items.name: PicoClaw
items.source_story_title: Why are AI agents lying, cheating and coordinating?
items.summary: A compact agent runtime built around small, composable tools.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly loved its bounded, boring-technology philosophy.
items.evidence: The endorsement praised PicoClaw's preference for simple, composable capabilities over complex machinery.

evidence_sources.author: schrodinger
evidence_sources.excerpt: This philosophy is what I love about PicoClaw

items.name: Persimmon
items.summary: A Humans& research model designed to simulate goal-directed human behavior.
items.why_included: A commenter recommended watching it as an early approach to human-aligned model training.
items.evidence: The commenter considered Persimmon potentially useful for teaching larger models to estimate human goals.

evidence_sources.author: lucrbvi
evidence_sources.excerpt: check out for the Persimmon model[0] from Humans&.

items.name: MESA
items.source_story_title: 'Fingerprints' inside the Sun could reveal if it once swallowed a planet
items.summary: An open-source suite for stellar evolution research and education.
items.why_included: A commenter gave unusually strong praise to its scientific community and impact.
items.evidence: The commenter described MESA as an incredible system whose importance exceeds ordinary software.

evidence_sources.author: mturk
evidence_sources.excerpt: MESA, a piece of software referenced in this article, is a pretty incredible system.

items.name: I Eat the Stars
items.source_story_title: Don't be the out of touch Kung Fu master
items.summary: Sarah Wilson's guide to living meaningfully amid systemic collapse.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly recommended it to people still seeking constructive responses.
items.evidence: The commenter directly recommended Sarah Wilson's book in a discussion about finding solutions.

evidence_sources.author: lowbloodsugar
evidence_sources.excerpt: I would like to recommend, to both of you, Sarah Wilson’s I Eat the Stars: How to Live Fully and Beautifully in a Collapsing World.

items.name: Connections Museum
items.summary: A Seattle museum preserving telecommunications equipment and switching technology.
items.why_included: A commenter directly recommended visiting it alongside Seattle's computer collections.
items.evidence: The commenter urged nearby readers to check out the museum.

evidence_sources.author: CircuitSeuss
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you’re in the area, check out the Connections Museum too!

items.name: Mimms Museum of Technology and Art
items.summary: An Atlanta-area museum devoted to vintage computing and technology artifacts.
items.why_included: A commenter praised it as a great museum for vintage-computing enthusiasts.
items.evidence: The recommendation highlighted its vintage-computing focus and artifacts inherited from the Living Computers Museum.

evidence_sources.author: nipmi
evidence_sources.excerpt: I know there's a great museum near Atlanta for those interested in vintage computing who live on the other side of the country

items.name: Australian Computer Museum Society
items.summary: A Sydney collection preserving and exhibiting historic computing technology.
items.why_included: A commenter directly recommended it to readers in Sydney.
items.evidence: The commenter singled out the Australian Computer Museum as a related place to visit.

evidence_sources.author: contingencies
evidence_sources.excerpt: In the same vein if you're in Sydney check out the Australian Computer Museum
